irregularities_flagged_for_review.title: Bridged sample_submission.tif mirrors labels.tif > 0 inside footprint
irregularities_flagged_for_review.detail: Measured 60,988 positive pixels inside sample_submission.tif with 0 pixel differences vs labels.tif > 0, whereas the DrivenData problem description describes an all-absence template. We use np.isfinite(sample_submission) strictly for the 5,167,373-pixel study-area footprint and never read sample_submission pixel values as features.

irregularities_flagged_for_review.title: USGS 1 m 3DEP LiDAR covers 75.40% of study footprint (24.60% NE/marginal gap)
irregularities_flagged_for_review.detail: Zero-filling missing LiDAR creates artificial probability cliffs along survey boundaries. Lane H82 passes native NaN to tree ensembles outside 1 m coverage, fuses full-footprint 3 m Wallace scarp diffusion + 10 m 3DEP breaklines + potential-field tilt, and applies per-quadrant non-LiDAR-to-LiDAR quantile calibration.

irregularities_flagged_for_review.title: Pigeonhole geometry on dense continuous maps and synthetic 5x5 calibration lattices in archive
irregularities_flagged_for_review.detail: Across all 1,026 historical TIFFs across 93 GEMSDOE repos, whole-footprint positive surfaces (e.g., 17GEMSDOE_E with 5,167,373 positive pixels = 100.0% of footprint) and synthetic 5-px regular grids (13gems_20261001_r13-lattice-s5_v2, 206,895 dots where max Euclidean distance from Z^2 to 5Z^2 is sqrt(2^2+2^2) = 2.8284 px < 3.0 px) cover 100.0% of interior Nevada within 3 px by pure Euclidean geometry. Both un-amended gems57/uniqueness.py forward overlap and mutual/sparse overlap are reported side by side.

irregularities_flagged_for_review.title: DrivenData '[0, 1]' range check & outside-footprint nodata handling
irregularities_flagged_for_review.detail: Prior submissions with unmasked NaNs or out-of-range float drift risked portal rejection ('Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]') or score degradation (0.2708 -nan vs 0.2778 -zeros on identical 37,654 dots). Our output enforces strict float32 values in {0.0, 1.0} across all 12,279,160 cells (0 NaNs, 0 Infs, nodata=None).
